gloss: to squeeze out; to wring out; to exploit

definitions.gloss: to squeeze out; to wring out
definitions.explanation: To physically extract liquid or substance by squeezing or wringing. Emphasizes thoroughness — getting every last drop.
To take money, labor, or resources from someone by coercion or unfair means. Carries a strongly negative connotation.

examples.japanese: レモンの{汁|しる}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る。
ぞうきんの{水|みず}を{最後|さいご}まで{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}った。
examples.english: I wrung out every last drop of water from the rag.

examples.japanese: {果物|くだもの}から{果汁|かじゅう}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}ってジュースにする。
examples.english: We squeeze the juice out of the fruit to make juice.

examples.japanese: {労働者|ろうどうしゃ}から{利益|りえき}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る。
examples.english: They exploit the workers for profit.

examples.japanese: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}から{大金|たいきん}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る{詐欺|さぎ}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Scams that squeeze large sums of money from elderly people are increasing.

examples.japanese: その{企業|きぎょう}は{下請|したう}け{業者|ぎょうしゃ}から{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}れるだけ{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}っている。
examples.english: That company is squeezing every last bit it can from its subcontractors.

notes:
Godan verb ({五段|ごだん}). Transitive.

A compound of {搾|しぼ}る (to squeeze) and {取|と}る (to take). The {取|と}る component adds the nuance of extraction — not just squeezing but actually getting something out.

ASPECT:
- {搾|しぼ}り{取|と}っている (is in the process of exploiting; has squeezed out)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {搾|しぼ}る means to squeeze but without the emphasis on extraction
- {搾取|さくしゅ}する is the more formal/political term for exploitation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {金|かね}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る (to squeeze money out of)
- {汁|しる}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る (to squeeze out the juice)
- {搾|しぼ}り{取|と}れるだけ{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る (to squeeze out as much as possible)
